The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/afb50fc9034d42ae57b9861dec4a2f5d0acf4f0c7122fc1ce845f5e3d60988fe.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=1$ and $x=4.$ Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should equal zero on both of these lines.

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{2}(1-x)(x-4) \\ {y}^{′} & =(1-x)(x-4)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=1$ and $x=4$ divide the plane into $3$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $3$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| Region | $x<1$ | $1<x<4$ | $x>4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slope | $↘$ | $↗$ | $↘$ |
| Sign | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

Of the three remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{2}(1-x)(x-4).
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{2}(1-x)(x-4).$
